answer: The attacker pays in compute, time, and reputation every time an alias is slashed, and these costs grow faster than the influence the cluster gains, making a large coordinated farm economically self-defeating. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. The system's strength comes from the fact that reputation is spent against performance, so a flood of accounts is filtered by the same economics that reward real work.
